data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The preference for better-corroborated theories is defensible on Popperian terms through the asymmetry of risk: rejecting a well-corroborated theory increases the likelihood of immediate error without offering compensatory testability, representing a logical deduction about the current state of knowledge rather than an inductive prediction.","counterconditions":[{"case":"refuted if it could be demonstrated that the concept of 'minimizing known unknowns' logically entails a probabilistic assessment of future performance, thereby collapsing the distinction between a deductive statement about past tests and an inductive expectation of future reliability","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"refuted if it can be shown that Popper explicitly justified the preference for better-corroborated theories in practical, life-or-death decisions on the grounds of safety or reliability rather than solely on the grounds of maximizing testability and information content","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"refuted if a formal proof shows one cannot quantify 'likelihood of immediate error' in a Popperian framework without invoking degrees of confirmation or probability","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Choosing the better-corroborated theory minimizes 'known unknowns' relative to alternatives; it is the theory that has not yet been falsified despite greater exposure. This is a defensive posture requiring no belief in future validity, only recognition of current robustness and the logical fact that the alternative has less empirical content or has failed tests the preferred theory survived.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
